prewrittenFacts.statement: The initial kitchen memory is from 1998.
The tin held buttons, not biscuits.
The lid had a crescent-shaped dent.
Mariam gave the tin to the younger sister, not the narrator.
The narrator cannot remember whether the departure memory was morning or the previous evening.

result.original: In 1998, my grandmother Mariam kept a blue tin on the highest shelf of her kitchen. It held spare buttons, not biscuits. The lid had a dent shaped like a crescent. Every Thursday, she let me choose one button and tell her where it might have come from. She never said the buttons were valuable. When she moved in 2006, my uncle Haris wanted to throw the tin away. Mariam gave it to my younger sister instead. I remember my sister carrying it with both hands, although I cannot remember whether that was the morning we left or the evening before. The tin stayed blue; nobody painted it. Years later, the thing I could still picture was the dent in the lid, not any of the stories I had invented about the buttons.
